text: QD3-009 answered by the handler on J's instruction (message of 2026-10-21T19:29Z; J, 21 Oct 21:21 Berlin): the re-check is a first batch. The Codex labeler account ran out of tokens. 472 rooms are accepted and compiled; of the 10 in UNRETURNED.tsv, nine were cut off mid-room (bangtan, furry_irl, germany, nerf, oneplus, placehearts, sixers, stlouis, yogscast) and traaaaaaannnnnnnnnns failed rule 6 and will be repaired; 223 rooms were not started. All 233 come as a second batch under the same handoff (VERSION 46384686) in two or three days. J's terms for this leg, which bind until the second batch: (1) adjudicate every re-check line of the 472 rooms; (2) move no model element: each move the evidence supports is written in notes-D3.md as a held proposal with its rooms and lines, and held until every room is back (section 2's re-examination is still made in the leg; only the move is held); (3) the 233 rooms are named pending, second batch, never unreturned, in every count and report; (4) D3c is not opened and nothing is frozen; D3b closes when the first batch is adjudicated and reopens for the second.

G61, the re-check rulings (logged at D3b, before any re-check line is ruled; section 6: every re-check line is adjudicated, and a completed re-check never silently accepts its lines; J's terms of QD3-009). The first batch is 472 rooms and 34,819 lines; the 233 other rooms are pending, second batch. (1) Repeats. A re-check line that repeats a first-return line of the same room exactly (the same element, the same op, the same cited codes, the same condition, statement and relation text, and for an absent line the same observation state) asks the same question of the same evidence. It takes the last ruling of the line it repeats, by an explicit ruling whose reason names that line, its decision and its kind; an accepted elaboration keeps its pair. A repeat whose match is ambiguous (two first-return lines with different rulings) is read, not ruled by reference. (2) Propose lines are all read: the fifteen candidates now stand in the model as candidates, so a proposal a candidate's statement or range states is held by it and rejected (G59a), and the rest are ruled under G59, G59a and their readings. A propose line that repeats one D3a-55 accepted for a candidate is held by that candidate. (3) Every other re-check line is read, by element group in packets of at most 100, under the G rules D3a used for its op (G1 to G60 as amended), against the revised statements; the candidates' lines are read the same way against the candidate's statement and range. An absent claim fails where the room's concepts show the element, and for a candidate that includes the codes of the room's own accepted D3a-55 proposal for it. (4) No move. Where two accepted corrections meet (section 2), the element is re-examined in the leg and the result is written in notes-D3.md as a held proposal with its rooms and lines; the model stays at 46384686... until the second batch is back. (5) Rulings are batched from files (QD3-001), checked by the batch adjudicator; a diary note names each file and its counts, and the ids stay in the files and the ledger.

slip, before any repeat ruling was written to the ledger: the first repeat files (d3_rulings/recheck-repeat-01 to -09.jsonl, 21,508 rows) would have accepted re-check lines that ingest marked NONPORTABLE where the line they repeat was accepted; the batch adjudicator refused the first file (4 such lines in it). G61 (1) reads with G6: such a repeat is a particular by construction. The builder now rules them so, and writes recheck-rep2-NN.jsonl; the first nine files stay unused.

G61's reading 1 (the re-check's absent lines, before their rows): G2 and G3 apply as at D3a. _analysis/d3b_absent_guard.py flags an unruled re-check absent line for reading when the room has an accepted or modified instantiate line on the element in either return (F1); for a candidate, when the room's D3a-55 proposal in its group was accepted or a D3a-56 residue names it (F2); when the line claims an evidenced absence (F3, read under G3); or when the room's placements carry the element, a second-order theme of the room on a third-order theme of the element's fourth-order tiers (F4, G2: the concepts are read first). Of 6,397 lines, 1,249 are flagged (F4 alone 1,138) and go to reading; the 5,148 others (unobserved 4,146, not-testable 1,002) are evidence limits under G2, accepted with kind none and counted apart, each reason saying that no accepted line, proposal or residue of the room shows the element. G61's reading 2 (the flagged re-check absent lines, before their rows): each flagged line is read in a packet of at most 100 (_analysis/d3b_packet.py: one element, in room order), with its cited concepts by label and, where a label leaves doubt, by quote through cite.py. G2 and G3 apply as at D3a. A line is rejected where its own concepts show the element as stated, and for a candidate that means its statement and range. An evidenced absence is a specification where the concepts show it and an evidence limit where they do not. The other lines are limits, accepted with kind none. A placement on the element's tier (F4) sends a line to reading, but it does not show the element alone: a placement is a theme on a node, and G2 reads the concepts. G6 rules a NONPORTABLE line first. _analysis/d3b_absent_rows.py rebuilds each packet and writes the default rulings, each naming the line's concepts; the read exceptions come from a rows file.
